title: Weekly sync
lines: Okay, let's start. Three things today: pricing for the Pro tier, the onboarding emails, and the finance comparison sheet.
On pricing, I looked at what the other note-taking tools charge and I think we should set the Pro tier at nine dollars a month.
Nine feels low to me, but it keeps us under the threshold where people ask their manager for approval.
Fine. Let's go with nine dollars a month for the Pro tier for now and revisit after launch.
I'll get the comparison sheet over to finance by Friday the fourth.
Good. Priya, where are the onboarding emails?
The first draft is rough. I want to rewrite the welcome email because it reads like a manual, nobody finishes it.
Agreed, the welcome email is the one that matters. How long will the rewrite take?
A week, maybe less if Dana helps with the layout.
Dana is busy with the pricing page design review on Friday, so probably not before then.
Then take the week. Anything else? No? Thanks everyone.

summary.overview: The team set the Pro tier at nine dollars a month and Sam will send finance a comparison sheet; Priya will rewrite the welcome email.

sections.heading: Pricing
sections.body: - Pro tier set at nine dollars a month, to be revisited after launch

actions.text: Send the comparison sheet to finance by Friday

title: Pricing page design review
lines: I brought two layouts for the pricing page. One has four panels across and one has three columns.
Four panels will be cramped on a laptop. The text for the Team plan alone is two lines.
I prefer the three columns. It reads more like a comparison and the price stands out.
Three columns it is. The Pro column gets the highlight because that is the one we want people to pick.
What about the main button? The mockup has it in orange.
Orange fights with our logo. I'd make the main button teal and keep orange only for warnings.
Teal works. Make the main button teal on the pricing page and on the sign-up page.
I'll deliver the full mockups by September eleventh.
Four panels would have looked busier anyway. Good call on the columns.
Great. Send the mockups to the channel when they're ready.

notes.text: Check contrast of teal button on white

title: Call with Orchard & Vane
lines: Thanks for making time, Ingrid. Tell me how the team has been finding Lumenpath.
Honestly, people like it. The summaries save us an hour a day. We have a hundred and forty seats at Orchard & Vane now.
That's great to hear. What would make it better for you?
Single sign-on. Our security group will not approve more seats without single sign-on.
Understood. We have a beta of single sign-on coming. I can promise you the SSO beta by the end of October.
End of October works. We'd like to be the first to try it.
You will be. I'll put your name on the list today.
One more thing, the export to our wiki loses the speaker names sometimes.
Noted. I'll pass that to Tomas, he's on exports.
Thank you, Sam. Talk again in October.

title: Sam and Alex 1:1
lines: Let's cover two things: the onboarding emails and whether we hire help.
Priya has been stretched with the billing work. I could take over the onboarding email rewrite from her.
Do it. Sam owns the onboarding email rewrite from now on. I'll tell Priya.
Okay. On hiring, I think one contractor for support and docs would help.
I agree. We'll hire one contractor for three months and see how it goes.
Do you have a budget in mind?
Not yet. Let's ask Dana and Tomas to interview candidates in October.
Sounds good. I'll write the job description.

title: Hosting call with Fennimore Cloud
lines: Thanks for joining. I'll walk through our plans. For your current usage the quote is four thousand two hundred dollars a month.
That's more than last quarter. The hosting bill keeps climbing as the transcripts pile up.
If you commit to an annual contract I can give you fifteen percent off.
I don't want to be locked in for a year while we still don't know our volumes. We'll stay on the monthly plan.
Can you send the contract so I can review the terms?
Then I'll review the contract by September twenty-fifth.
Marcus, does the monthly plan include the storage tier?
Storage is billed separately, about three hundred a month at your size.

summary.overview: Fennimore quoted 4,200 dollars a month for hosting with 15 percent off for an annual contract; Alex chose to stay on the monthly plan.

sections.heading: Hosting
sections.body:
- Quote of 4,200 dollars a month
- Annual discount of 15 percent declined

actions.text: Review the Fennimore contract by September 25

title: Weekly sync
lines: The big item is the launch date. The single sign-on beta is slipping, and we promised it to Orchard.
If we hold the twentieth of October, we ship without it. I'd rather move the launch.
Then we move it. The launch is now November third, up from October twentieth.
That gives me time on the export bug. It's top priority before the launch, because exports lose speaker names.
Agreed, the export bug comes before everything else. Tomas, when?
I'll fix the export bug by October seventh.
I'll send the onboarding email draft on October second.
I'm still on the email rewrite, so Priya, send me your notes on the welcome email and I'll fold them in.

summary.overview: The launch moved from October 20 to November 3 because the SSO beta slipped; fixing the export bug is the top priority.

actions.text: Fix the export bug by October 7
Send the onboarding email draft on October 2

title: Third quarter retro
lines: Let's do the retro for the third quarter. What went well?
Three things stand out: faster releases, support response under four hours, and the new docs site.
I'd add that the docs site cut the questions we get about setup.
The outages. We had two outages, one on the twelfth of September and one on the twenty-seventh.
Both were during working hours, so customers noticed.
We need alerting that pages someone sooner. Tomas, can you look at it?
On the offsite, we should think about where.
Let's leave that for November. Thanks, everyone.

title: Call with Kestrel Logistics
lines: Thanks for the call. We've used Lumenpath for a year at Kestrel Logistics and the team likes it. We pay six thousand a year.
Glad to hear it. What are you missing?
An audit log. Our compliance people need to see who opened and exported which transcript. Without an audit trail, we'll look elsewhere at renewal.
That's very reasonable. I'll have an audit log spec to you by October twenty-first.
That would help. We'd also like longer retention for exports.
I'll add that to the spec as well.
Thank you. Renewal is in January, so we have a little time.

notes.text: Kestrel is a churn risk without the audit log

title: Pricing review
lines: We've been at nine dollars for six weeks. Sam, what does the data say?
Sign-up interest is fine, but at nine dollars we are leaving money on the table. Customers compare us to tools that charge fifteen.
Our support cost per user is higher than nine dollars covers, honestly.
A higher price also makes the pricing page look less like a bargain bin.
Then let's change it. We're setting the Pro tier at twelve dollars a month, starting November third, replacing the nine dollar price.
Team stays at thirty dollars per seat.
I'll update the billing configuration by October twenty-eighth.
I'll move the comparison sheet to the board pack instead of finance, since the board asks about pricing.
Good. Dana, the pricing page needs the new number before the launch.

summary.overview: The Pro tier price changes from nine to twelve dollars a month starting November 3; Team stays at thirty dollars per seat.

sections.heading: Decisions
sections.body: - Pro tier at twelve dollars a month from November 3

actions.text: Update the billing configuration by October 28
Move the comparison sheet to the board pack

title: Weekly sync
lines: Quick status. The single sign-on beta went to Orchard and Vane yesterday, on the twentieth.
They already logged in with it. Ingrid says it works.
And the launch is still November third, nothing changes there.
The export bug is fixed and shipped. Speaker names survive now.
About the audit log spec for Kestrel, I need a few more days. I'll have it done by Friday the twenty-third.
Fine, tell Noor it's slipping two days.
The billing configuration for the new price is on track for next week.

summary.overview: SSO beta reached Orchard; the launch stays November 3; Sam moved the audit log spec to Friday the 23rd.

sections.heading: Status
sections.body:
- Launch date unchanged
- Export bug fixed

actions.text: Deliver the audit log spec by Friday the 23rd

title: Contractor interview debrief
lines: We interviewed three people for the contractor role. Dana, your impressions?
Rowan was the strongest. Clear writing, and she had already read our docs site and found two errors.
I agree. Rowan's support examples were concrete. The other two were more generic.
Then we make an offer to Rowan. Seven thousand five hundred dollars a month for the three months.
I'll send the offer tomorrow. If she accepts she starts on the second of November.
I'll prepare her laptop and accounts.

title: Call with Harrowgate Bank
lines: We're evaluating Lumenpath for the compliance team at Harrowgate Bank. We're looking at two other vendors as well.
Thanks for including us. What matters most to you?
Everything has to stay in a Canadian data center. We cannot have recordings crossing the border.
We can host Harrowgate's data in the Canadian region. That's possible with our setup.
Good. We also have a security questionnaire, four pages.
Send it over. I'll send the security questionnaire answers by November sixth.
That works. Our review meets the week after.
Then you'll have it in time.

summary.overview: Harrowgate Bank is comparing three vendors and needs data to stay in Canada; Sam will answer their security questionnaire by November 6.

sections.heading: Requirements
sections.body: - Data must stay in a Canadian data center

actions.text: Send the security questionnaire answers by November 6

title: Priya and Alex 1:1
lines: How are you doing, really? The launch week was heavy.
Honestly, I'm wiped out. I haven't had a real break since August and I need a week off the week of Thanksgiving.
Take it. I'll cover the billing questions that week.
Thank you. Sam is traveling next week, so the Harrowgate questionnaire answers are going to slip.
I'll take the Harrowgate questionnaire from Sam and finish it by Thursday.
Great. Let's tell Sam so he knows it's off his plate.

title: Launch retro
lines: The launch happened on Tuesday. Let's see the numbers.
We had four hundred and twelve sign-ups in the first two days.
And churn went from four percent to three point two after the new onboarding emails.
No outages during launch week, which is the first time.
I spotted a typo on the pricing page. It says 'recieve' under the Team plan.
I'll push the patch by November ninth.
Good. Overall, a good launch. Let's keep the momentum.

bookmarks.text: Typo on pricing page: fix before the weekend

title: Weekly sync
lines: We have to talk about the Pro tier. Customers who joined at nine dollars are complaining about the increase.
We can keep it simple. New customers pay twelve dollars. Existing customers stay at nine dollars until March.
Okay. Existing customers keep nine dollars until March, and then they move to twelve.
I'll adjust the billing system again, then.
Kestrel renewed, by the way. They signed for two years.
Wonderful news. Who sends the paperwork?
I'll send the renewal paperwork by November twentieth.
Orchard and Vane also went up to two hundred seats.
That's thirty percent more load on exports.

summary.overview: Existing Pro customers keep nine dollars until March; Kestrel renewed for two years and Orchard expanded to two hundred seats.

sections.heading: Pricing
sections.body: - Existing customers stay at nine dollars until March

actions.text: Send the Kestrel renewal paperwork by November 20

title: Offsite planning
lines: Time to settle the offsite. Where do we go?
Tallinn is cheap in winter and the flights from here are fine. I'd pick Tallinn.
I like it. The old town is great and it's walkable.
Then it's decided: the offsite is in Tallinn, February ninth to twelfth.
Eleven people. Dana, can you handle the venue?
I'll book the venue by November twenty-fifth.

title: Call with Tidewell Foods
lines: We have sixty seats at Tidewell Foods and half of our kitchen managers speak Spanish.
Do they need transcripts in Spanish?
Yes. They record in Spanish and want the transcript and summary in Spanish too.
We're working on it. I'll promise you Spanish transcripts by the end of January.
That would be a big help. Can we try a beta?
Sure, I'll add you to the beta list.
Thanks. We'll look forward to it.

title: Support triage
lines: We had thirty-seven tickets last week. The top three issues were login loops, export timeouts, and billing emails.
How many P1 bugs are open right now?
Seven open P1 bugs, most of them in exports.
That's too many. Let's rotate support. We'll run a weekly support rotation, starting with Noor.
Fine with me. I'll take this week.
I'll write down the runbook so the rotation is easy.

title: Evening call
lines: How's work? You sounded stressed last time.
It's fine. Honestly, I've been thinking about leaving Lumenpath in the spring and moving to Montreal.
No, and please don't mention it. I'll decide after the offsite.
Your secret is safe. Montreal is cold, though.

title: Notes to self
lines: Reminder: my dentist appointment is on November twenty-fourth at three in the afternoon.
Also, I should buy a gift for my sister. Budget around eighty dollars.
